id: simple
name: Simple Pipeline
extends: null

# ADR-037 §4: per-template merge policy. Wired to runtime behavior in #975.
merge_policy: auto_unless_flagged

# #2367: the run's branch; {key} is the run's identity (issue-<n>). A repository
# overrides it in .zbuild/branch; ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH overrides both.
branch: zbuild/{key}

defaults:
  strategy: map

# ─── Flow ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Simplified pipeline (ADR-037 EPIC #966 / ADR-040 EPIC #1129): 7 top-level flow
# units — intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
# OVER convergence from the retired monolithic objective-gate to the composable
# mechanical gates; the objective-gate plugin was then removed in B7 (#1139).
# #2368: the engine combines the gates by build_test_cycle's exit_when, which
# names every member that must pass; gate-aggregator is retired.
#
# C3 (#1142, ADR-040 §3 — supersedes ADR-038's single-stage fan-out; ADR-039
# parallel group; follows ADR-030 scope governance) CUTS OVER the lens side: the
# monolithic `review` stage (ADR-038's hand-rolled review-report fan-out, now
# UNREFERENCED here) is replaced by `review_lenses` — a `type: map over: lenses`
# `aggregate: advisory` group (issue #1295, ADR-047 §2; was `type: parallel`) —
# one work unit per lens element. #2368: the engine sums the lenses up
# (review_lenses-summary.md) and says whether one was flagged
# (ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED); review-aggregator is retired. The lens group is
# ADVISORY: it NEVER feeds the cycle's
# exit_when/convergence (build_test_cycle's exit_when, ADR-040 §5) and never
# blocks merge. The B5 no-LLM-on-convergence-path invariant therefore holds.
flow:
  - hydrate
  - intake
  - plan
  - delivery_loop
  - review_lenses
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
# timeout — in the order listed, after the flow has ended.
#
# This replaces a hardcoded dispatch in the runner's EXIT trap, which named one
# plugin by DIRECTORY (`plugins/tool/teardown`) and degraded silently to a no-op
# if it was absent. "Runs on every exit path" is a property of the FLOW, so it
# belongs in the template that defines the flow — not at a line number inside a
# 3000-line runner, where an edit can drop it without anything noticing. #1878
# found exactly that failure in the sibling mechanism: the snapshot was never
# called.
#
# An always-run stage is NOT part of `flow:` and never enters the flow's stage
# list: it has no place in the pipeline's data dependencies and must not affect
# convergence, verdicts, or the run's exit status.
#
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `router.timeout_s`. A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release
  - persist

# ─── delivery_loop (cycle) — #2271, ADR-068 ─────────────────────────────────
# One outer loop holds design and the build loop. Every stage sees every
# finding and says in its own result what it did about each; the engine never
# decides who owns a finding, and nothing jumps backwards.
#   - design makes one model call per run and checks the design it wrote. One
#     that fails is `unusable`: the engine runs design again (its retry:), and
#     each run starts from the last good design and the last try's failures
#     (ADR-068 §8). A design that still fails ends the run — stop_run_on_fail:
#     build never runs on it, and another round would only repeat those tries.
delivery_loop:
  type: cycle
  description: Design, then build, until both pass — going round when a finding needs design
  flow:
    - design
    - build_test_cycle
  exit_when:
    all:
      - { stage: design, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
      - { stage: build_test_cycle, field: verdict, op: eq, value: pass }
  stop_run_on_fail: [design]
  max_iterations: 2
  on_max: halt

# ─── test-author (leaf, build_test_cycle member; the loop requires it) ───────
# ADR-040 §5: it makes a model call, so it may not sit on the convergence path.
# Its work is verified mechanically downstream — the test stage runs the
# assertions and acceptance-gate proves they discriminate.
test-author:
  gate: auto
  roles: [test_author]
  # The whole stage, every call and check inside it (4 model calls of 15 minutes, plus a few minutes); the engine
  # stops it here. The default for a stage is 900 (15 minutes).
  timeout_s: 3780
  # #2188: no authored assertions → the cycle stops before build. Otherwise build
  # writes its own tests, the defect #2022 exists to prevent (#1849 run
  # 35949629759). Its failure is retried first (the stage's `retry:` budget).
  blocking: true
  router:
    # #2188: the same budget as build — authoring a 15–25 SPEC contract is
    # build-sized work (#1849: two 600s calls both timed out mid-write).
    # #2225: per CALL now — test-author loops until it says it is done, like
    # build, so a big contract takes more calls instead of overrunning one.
    # At most 4 calls: timeouts that are not back-to-back let the loop go on,
    # so the ceiling is calls × timeout — 60 min here (review #2229).
    timeout_s: 900
    max_turns: 0
    max_iterations: 4

# #1849: the finished change against the ISSUE. A model call on the convergence
# path is allowed for the same reason as design's coverage check (ADR-040 §5 as amended by

issue-acceptance:
  gate: auto
  roles: [issue_acceptance]

  # delivered?" — now asked of the code.
  persona: product-owner
  router:
    timeout_s: 600

    # requires it to pass — the SPEC is design's, which it cannot re-author.
    - test-author
    # #2371: build scans its own change for secrets (was a stage of its own).
    - build
    - test
    # #1849: the finished change judged against the ISSUE, not the SPECs — the
    # only check after design's own coverage check that reads the issue; each unmet

    - issue-acceptance

  io:

    tail_lines: 200

# Convergence is owned by build_test_cycle's exit_when above;

      persona: scope
    - id: sre

# ─── pr (leaf) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  roles: [teardown]

# process-group kill does not.

  gate: auto

# stage's prior-output seam can seed from earlier work. Runs BEFORE intake, and

id: always-run-minimal
name: Always-Run Minimal Pipeline
extends: simple
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

# #1831 fixture: the smallest template that exercises `always_run:`.
#
# NEW shape (`flow:` + top-level sections) on purpose — but NOT because
# `always_run:` needs it. The key is shape-INDEPENDENT: `_tpl_parse_always_run`
# reads it straight from the file, and SPEC-6 in tests/unit/template-always-run-test.sh
# proves an old-shape template inherits it too. The new shape is used here only
# because it is the smaller fixture, and because it exercises the per-repo
# overlay's new-shape path alongside it.
#
# `outcome` is the only flow stage. Its plugin is replaced per-case by the test
# so one fixture can drive every exit path: rc=0, rc=1, SIGINT (rc=130), SIGTERM
# and a hang past the timeout. `release` is never in the flow — the whole point
# is that it runs anyway.
flow:
  - outcome

always_run:
  - release

outcome:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

# timeout_s is deliberately small so the watchdog case does not stretch the
# suite's wall clock. The bound itself is what SPEC-5 asserts.
release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  timeout_s: 2
  router:
    timeout_s: 2
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

main() {
    local issue="" goal="" dry_run=false template="simple"
    local resume_mode=false from_stage="" no_resume=false force=false
    # #963: self-host mode — redirect read-only contract-grammar libs to a
    # working-tree snapshot. Honors ZBUILD_SELF_HOST=1 (resolved after parse).
    local self_host=false

    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            --issue)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--issue requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                issue="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --goal)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--goal requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                goal="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --template)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--template requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                template="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --dry-run)    dry_run=true;    shift ;;
            --resume)     resume_mode=true; shift ;;
            --no-resume)  no_resume=true;  shift ;;
            --force)      force=true;      shift ;;
            --self-host)  self_host=true;  shift ;;
            --from-stage)
                [[ -z "${2:-}" ]] && { error "--from-stage requires a value"; _usage; return 1; }
                from_stage="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --help|-h)  _usage; return 0 ;;
            *) error "Unknown argument: $1"; _usage; return 1 ;;
        esac
    done

    # #963: ZBUILD_SELF_HOST=1 is equivalent to the --self-host flag.
    [[ "${ZBUILD_SELF_HOST:-0}" == "1" ]] && self_host=true
    # #2225: the run's resume intent reaches every stage as ZBUILD_RESUME —
    # 1 (reuse prior work) unless --no-resume, and ZBUILD_RESUME=0 in the
    # environment is the same as the flag. Each stage decides what reuse means
    # for it; hydrate restores nothing under 0.
    ZBUILD_RESUME="$(_runner_resume_intent "$no_resume")"
    export ZBUILD_RESUME
    [[ "$ZBUILD_RESUME" == "0" ]] && no_resume=true

    if [[ -z "$issue" && -z "$goal" ]]; then
        error "Must specify --issue <N> or --goal \"<text>\""
        _usage
        return 1
    fi

    # --from-stage is only valid in resume mode
    if [[ -n "$from_stage" ]] && ! $resume_mode; then
        error "--from-stage is only valid with --resume"
        _usage
        return 1
    fi

    local plugins_root="${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}"
    # #1614: fill the manifest cache HERE, in main()'s own shell. yaml_get was
    # 6,338 awk spawns per run (~13s of 27s); most call sites read it inside $( ),
    # and a cache written in a command substitution dies with that subshell — so
    # the fill has to happen in a shell that every later subshell descends from.
    # Cheap no-op when the cache is disabled or the root does not exist.

if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
    fi
    local state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-${ZBUILD_STATE_ROOT:-$HOME/.zbuild/state}}"
    # #887: when neither ZBUILD_STATE_DIR nor ZBUILD_STATE_FILE is set, a fresh
    # run roots its state under runs/<run_id>/ so concurrent runs never share a
    # state dir / artifacts. Explicit overrides (tests, CLI resume) win and skip
    # the re-root. Resolved here; applied once run_id is known (fresh-start block).
    local _state_is_default=false
    [[ -z "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" && -z "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE:-}" ]] && _state_is_default=true
    local template_file
    # Per-repo overrides live under the target repo's working tree (#653/#724
    # Copilot finding): use $PWD, not $_ZBUILD_ROOT (the install tree).
    if ! template_file="$(resolve_template_file "$template" "$PWD" 2>&1)"; then
        error "$template_file"
        return 1
    fi

    # Cross-check: ZBUILD_STATE_FILE vs --issue (issue #296 Δ-4)
    # Placed before --dry-run so dry-run also surfaces mismatches.
    # Fail-closed on corrupt state files (rather than letting get_state_field
    # silently return its default and skip the check).
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE:-}" && -n "$issue" && "$issue" != "0" \
          && -f "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE}" ]]; then
        if ! jq empty "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            error "ZBUILD_STATE_FILE='${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE}' is not valid JSON; refusing to honor it alongside --issue $issue (fail-closed)"
            return 1
        fi
        local _existing_issue
        _existing_issue="$(jq -r '.issue // ""' "${ZBUILD_STATE_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [[ -n "$_existing_issue" && "$_existing_issue" != "null" \
              && "$_existing_issue" != "0" && "$_existing_issue" != "$issue" ]]; then
            error "ZBUILD_STATE_FILE points at run for issue $_existing_issue but --issue is $issue (mismatch); aborting to avoid silent override"
            return 1
        fi
    fi

    # Load template. All three failure modes fail closed (#1283, ADR-047 §6 — the
    # mechanic no longer carries a hardcoded built-in stage roster):
    #   - template FILE missing (resolve_template_file returns a non-existent
    #     path) → error, abort (rc=2).
    #   - file EXISTS but load_template fails → a genuine config error, e.g. an
    #     invalid merge_policy enum (#1057 review): surface its stderr (no
    #     2>/dev/null) and abort.
    #   - loads cleanly but defines no stages → malformed template, abort.
    local active_stages=()
    if [[ ! -f "$template_file" ]]; then
        # ADR-047 §6: fail-closed. The old built-in fallback list hardcoded stage
        # names (intake security-lens output — `output` was never a real stage) in
        # the mechanic. A run/preview needs a valid template; a missing one is a
        # config error, not a silent bogus roster. (No --template defaults to the
        # shipped `simple` template, which resolves; this branch fires only on an
        # explicitly-named template whose file is absent.)
        error "Template '$template' not found (no file at '$template_file'); cannot run without a valid template — check the --template name or install the template"
        return 1
    elif ! load_template "$template_file"; then
        error "Failed to load template '$template' (see error above); aborting"
        return 1
    elif [[ ${#_TPL_STAGES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
        active_stages=("${_TPL_STAGES[@]}")

#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
_orch_find_backend_dir() {
    local alias="$1"
    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"

    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1

    local manifest plugin_dir
    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
        # Check provides.role
        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
            continue
        fi
        # Check id or provides.alias match
        local id declared_alias
        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
            echo "$plugin_dir"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)

    return 1
}

# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
# No fallback: a missing or unreadable backend is a hard misconfigured error.
orch_load_backend() {
    local backend="${1:-}"
    local plugin_dir

    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
                warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
                _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
                return 1
            fi
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # Last-resort: try the built-in bash-parallel backend by its known repo path (#1801).
    # This resolves the default even when ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT does not include the
    # installed orch backends (common in integration tests that override ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT).
    # Only bash-parallel gets this treatment — it is the declared system default; any other
    # backend that reaches this point is truly misconfigured.
    local _bash_parallel_sh="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/plugin.sh"
    if [[ "$backend" == "bash-parallel" && -f "$_bash_parallel_sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "$_bash_parallel_sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "$_bash_parallel_sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # No plugin found — hard misconfigured error naming the backend.
    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found — misconfigured (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias '${backend}')" || true
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.

# ─── setup_git_temp_repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Creates a real, minimal git repo under $TEST_TEMP_DIR/<name> with one
# initial commit. Returns its absolute path on stdout. Used by integration
# tests that exercise real `git checkout`/`git symbolic-ref` against an
# isolated repo (issue #484).
#
# Usage:
#   repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo myrepo)"
#   (cd "$repo" && some_test)
setup_git_temp_repo() {
    local name="${1:-gitrepo}"
    local repo="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/$name"
    mkdir -p "$repo" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    (
        # #2103 / ADR-024: the cd MUST be fatal. `set -e` is inert inside this
        # subshell because its status is tested by `|| return 1` below, so a
        # failed cd would otherwise run every git command in the CALLER'S
        # checkout — which is exactly what committed seed.txt into a real
        # worktree and pushed a branch to the real origin on 2026-09-15.
        cd "$repo" || exit 1
        # Use the real git binary (not whatever PATH shim may be present).
        local real_git
        real_git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || true)"
        # If a shim like the parity-fixture mock is on PATH, fall back to
        # well-known absolute locations.
        if [[ -z "$real_git" ]]; then
            for c in /usr/bin/git /usr/local/bin/git /opt/homebrew/bin/git; do
                [[ -x "$c" ]] && real_git="$c" && break
            done
        fi
        [[ -z "$real_git" ]] && return 1
        "$real_git" init -q -b main 2>/dev/null || "$real_git" init -q
        "$real_git" config user.email "test@zbuild.local"
        "$real_git" config user.name "zbuild-test"
        "$real_git" config commit.gpgsign false
        echo "seed" > seed.txt
        "$real_git" add seed.txt
        "$real_git" commit -q -m "seed"
        # Normalize default branch name to 'main' for predictable tests.
        local cur
        cur="$("$real_git" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main)"
        if [[ "$cur" != "main" ]]; then
            "$real_git" branch -m "$cur" main 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$repo"
}

# ── setup_git_master_origin (#2103) ──────────────────────────────────────────
# A bare origin whose default branch is `master` (not `main`), seeded with one
# commit, plus a working clone of it whose origin/HEAD → origin/master. Prints
# the clone's path; prints nothing and returns 1 on any setup failure. Extracted
# from tests/integration/intake-branch-ahead-count-test.sh, where a failed seed
# clone let the seeding subshell run — and `git push origin HEAD:master` — in
# the caller's checkout against the caller's origin. Every cd here is fatal
# because each subshell's status is tested (see setup_git_temp_repo).
#
# Usage:
#   clone="$(setup_git_master_origin a)" || fail "setup"
setup_git_master_origin() {
    local label="${1:-m}"
    local bare="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bare-${label}.git"
    local work="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/work-${label}"
    local tmp_init="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/init-${label}"

    git init --bare "$bare" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
    git -C "$bare" symbolic-ref HEAD "refs/heads/master" 2>/dev/null || { printf ''; return 1; }

    # Seed via a throwaway clone. The clone's OWN rc is checked before the
    # subshell so a clone failure never reaches the cd; the cd is fatal anyway.
    git clone "$bare" "$tmp_init" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
    (
        cd "$tmp_init" || exit 1
        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
        # Unborn HEAD: -b names the branch regardless of init.defaultBranch.
        git checkout -q -b master 2>/dev/null || git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/master || exit 1
        echo "seed" > seed.txt || exit 1
        git add seed.txt || exit 1
        git commit -q -m "seed" || exit 1
        git push -q origin HEAD:"refs/heads/master" || exit 1
    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
    rm -rf "$tmp_init"

    # The bare repo MUST now carry master; a bare `.git` check downstream cannot
    # tell "seeded" from "empty", and an unborn HEAD makes `checkout master` a no-op.
    git -C "$bare" show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/master || { printf ''; return 1; }

    git clone "$bare" "$work" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }
    (
        cd "$work" || exit 1
        git config user.email "test@zbuild.local" || exit 1
        git config user.name "zbuild-test" || exit 1
        git config commit.gpgsign false || exit 1
    ) >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf ''; return 1; }

    printf '%s\n' "$work"
}

# ── install_template_overlay (#1270) ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Copy one or more template fixtures into a repo's per-repo override dir
# (<repo>/.zbuild/templates/<id>.yaml), the generic ADR-016 overlay seam. A test
# that then runs the engine with CWD = <repo> resolves the fixture WITHOUT any
# env var and WITHOUT writing into the tracked config/templates/ — the overlay
# lives entirely inside the test's temp repo (reaped by the master EXIT/INT/TERM
# trap). This replaces the #1268 ZBUILD_TEMPLATES_DIR seam (reverted in #1270):
# no ambient env, no global state; hermeticity comes from CWD isolation.
#
# Each fixture is a `.zbuild/templates/` overlay, so it MUST carry `extends: <id>`
# (ADR-016). The shipped base it extends (usually `simple`) is read from the
# engine tree unchanged — only the overlay id needs a fixture.
#
# Usage: install_template_overlay <repo> <id> [<id> ...]
# install_simple_loop_continue <repo> — overlay template `simple-loop-continue`:
# the shipped simple.yaml with delivery_loop set to on_max: continue.
# #2241: simple.yaml's outer loop is on_max: halt, and the runner honours it.
# Tests whose subject is the CONTINUE path past an exhausted loop (#766, #1217)
# drive this instead — generated from the real template at test time, so it
# never drifts from it. (#2369: the design loop it once also changed is retired.)
install_simple_loop_continue() {
    local _repo="${1:?install_simple_loop_continue: <repo> required}" _src_root
    _src_root="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)"
    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
    awk '
        /^id: simple$/ { print "id: simple-loop-continue"; print "extends: simple"; next }
        /^delivery_loop:/ { in_dl = 1; print; next }
        in_dl && /^[a-z_-]+:/ { in_dl = 0 }
        in_dl && /^  on_max: halt$/ { print "  on_max: continue"; next }
        { print }
    ' "$_src_root/config/templates/simple.yaml" > "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml"
    grep -q '^id: simple-loop-continue$' "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/simple-loop-continue.yaml" || return 1
    # Committed, as install_template_overlay_committed does: an untracked
    # overlay leaves the tree dirty and intake refuses to start on it.
    local _git; _git="$(command -v git 2>/dev/null || echo /usr/bin/git)"
    "$_git" -C "$_repo" add .zbuild/templates >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    "$_git" -C "$_repo" commit -q -m "add test template overlay" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
}

install_template_overlay() {
    local _repo="$1"; shift
    # Fail fast on an empty repo arg (e.g. an unset OVERLAY_REPO): otherwise we'd
    # mkdir/cp into /.zbuild/templates and fail later with a confusing error.
    if [[ -z "$_repo" ]]; then
        echo "install_template_overlay: <repo> argument required (got empty)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    mkdir -p "$_repo/.zbuild/templates"
    # The overlay is test setup, not work: kept out of `git status` so the
    # engine's dirty-tree check (#2367) does not refuse the run.
    if [[ -d "$_repo/.git/info" ]] && ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
        printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_repo/.git/info/exclude"
    fi
    # Repo root derived from THIS helper's location (…/scripts/lib → repo root),
    # not the caller's cwd, so it resolves regardless of where the test runs.
    local _hdir _src_root
    _hdir="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
    _src_root="$(cd "$_hdir/../.." && pwd)"
    local _id _src
    for _id in "$@"; do
        _src="$_src_root/tests/fixtures/templates/${_id}.yaml"
        if [[ ! -f "$_src" ]]; then
            echo "install_template_overlay: fixture not found: $_src" >&2
            return 1
        fi
        cp "$_src" "$_repo/.zbuild/templates/${_id}.yaml"
    done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
#
# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
#
#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
#
# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1

# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
else
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
fi

_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)

# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
_orch_not_implemented() {
    local fn_name="$1"
    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
    fi
    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.

if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
fi

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend

## What was fixed in Round 12

### Fix 1: SPEC-1 — orch-timeout-applies-test.sh (SPEC-1f/g/h)

**Problem**: SPEC-1f, 1g, and 1h checked `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME` but that variable
is never set by either old or new code. Both old and new code leave it empty, so
the test fails on BOTH old and new code (acceptance check: "does not pass on new code").

**Root cause**: The SPEC says "the test for each strategy verifies the outcome variable
`_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME` is set to `timed_out` (not `failed`)". The phrase "not `failed`"
means OLD code sets `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="failed"` on non-zero collect rc. NEW code
preserves `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="timed_out"` from the collect result.

**Fix**: Changed all three (fanout, sequential, map) to check `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME`
instead of `_ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME`:
- Initialize `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME=""` before the strategy call (reset)
- Mock `orch_collect` sets `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="timed_out"` and returns 1
- OLD code: strategy resets `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME` to `"failed"` → test fails ✓
- NEW code: strategy preserves `_ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME="timed_out"` → test passes ✓

### Fix 2: SPEC-7 — lint-adr-enforced-by-test.sh

**Problem**: Round-2 checker finding: "assertions verify only that an `## Enforced by`
heading exists and section contains at least one `tests/` reference, but do not verify
that every individual statement (§) is mapped to a test".

**Fix**: Replaced the "at least one tests/ reference" checks with per-statement
coverage checks using awk:
- `awk '/^## Enforced by/{p=1;next} /^## /{p=0} p && /^- §/ && !/tests\//{print}'`
  → extracts `- §` lines in Enforced by that LACK a `tests/` reference (unmapped)
- `awk '/^## Enforced by/{p=1;next} /^## /{p=0} p && /^- §/{c++} END{print c+0}'`
  → counts total `- §` lines in the section
- Asserts: count > 0 AND all §-lines have `tests/` (unmapped list is empty)
- Applied to both ADR-011 and ADR-017

the code author implements always_run persist dispatch. CORRECT.

# ── SPEC-4 static: runner.sh gates on _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION ────────
# runner.sh must check _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION immediately after
# sourcing contract.sh and exit 1 naming the backend when the disposition is
# `misconfigured`, before dispatching any stage.
#
# Old code: no such check in runner.sh → grep fails → assertion FAILS on old code.
# New code: the check exists → grep succeeds → assertion PASSES.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-4] static: runner.sh contains _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION gate"

if grep -q '_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION' "$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] runner.sh contains _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION gate (checked after contract.sh)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] runner.sh must check _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION after sourcing contract.sh" \
        "grep found no _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION in runner.sh; old code has no disposition gate"
fi

# ── SPEC-4 e2e: absent backend fails full pipeline run as misconfigured ───────
# Create a minimal installed tree (rsync), remove orch-bash-parallel from it,
# then run bash $ZBUILD_HOME/core/pipeline/runner.sh. With _ZBUILD_ROOT pointing
# at the temp install, the last-resort check ($ZBUILD_HOME/plugins/tool/orch-bash-
# parallel/plugin.sh) also fails — so both the registry path and last resort agree
# the backend is absent.
#
# Old code: runner.sh ignores _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION → continues →
#   eventually fails with "orch_spawn: not implemented" or similar (not "misconfigured").
# New code: runner.sh gates early → exits 1 with "misconfigured" naming the backend.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: absent backend fails pipeline as misconfigured"

if ! command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    printf '  \033[38;2;250;204;21mSKIP\033[0m: [#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: rsync not available\n' >&2
else
    _E2E_S4_INSTALL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-install-spec4"
    mkdir -p "$_E2E_S4_INSTALL"
    rsync -aL --quiet \
        "$REPO_ROOT/core" \
        "$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
        "$REPO_ROOT/config" \
        "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" \
        "$_E2E_S4_INSTALL/"
    # Remove the default backend from the temp install so both the registry scan
    # and the bash-parallel last-resort check fail.
    rm -rf "$_E2E_S4_INSTALL/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel"

    _E2E_S4_STATE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-s4-state"
    _E2E_S4_EVDIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-s4-events"
    mkdir -p "$_E2E_S4_STATE" "$_E2E_S4_EVDIR"
    _E2E_S4_RC=0
    _E2E_S4_OUT="$(
        ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$_E2E_S4_STATE" \
        ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$_E2E_S4_EVDIR" \
        ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$_E2E_S4_EVDIR/events.jsonl" \
        ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
        ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
        ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
        bash "$_E2E_S4_INSTALL/core/pipeline/runner.sh" \
            --template simple --goal "e2e-spec4-absent" 2>&1
    )" || _E2E_S4_RC=$?

    if [[ "$_E2E_S4_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: absent backend causes pipeline to exit non-zero"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: absent backend must cause pipeline to exit non-zero" \
            "runner exited 0; expected non-zero when backend missing from installed tree"
    fi

    if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_E2E_S4_OUT"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: pipeline output names absent backend as 'misconfigured'"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: pipeline output must name absent backend as 'misconfigured'" \
            "output did not contain 'misconfigured'; old code: no runner.sh gate, orch_spawn stub fires with 'not implemented' instead; got: ${_E2E_S4_OUT:0:300}"
    fi

    if grep -q 'bash-parallel' <<< "$_E2E_S4_OUT"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: pipeline output names the missing backend 'bash-parallel'"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] e2e: pipeline output must name the missing backend" \
            "output did not contain 'bash-parallel'; got: ${_E2E_S4_OUT:0:300}"
    fi

# ── SPEC-10 e2e: unreadable plugin.sh fails full pipeline run as misconfigured ─

print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: unreadable plugin.sh fails pipeline as misconfigured"

if ! command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    printf '  \033[38;2;250;204;21mSKIP\033[0m: [#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: rsync not available\n' >&2
else
    _E2E_S10_INSTALL="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-install-spec10"
    mkdir -p "$_E2E_S10_INSTALL"
    rsync -aL --quiet \
        "$REPO_ROOT/core" \
        "$REPO_ROOT/plugins" \
        "$REPO_ROOT/config" \
        "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" \
        "$_E2E_S10_INSTALL/"
    # Make orch-bash-parallel's plugin.sh unreadable.
    chmod 000 "$_E2E_S10_INSTALL/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/plugin.sh"

    _E2E_S10_STATE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-s10-state"
    _E2E_S10_EVDIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/e2e-s10-events"
    mkdir -p "$_E2E_S10_STATE" "$_E2E_S10_EVDIR"
    _E2E_S10_RC=0
    _E2E_S10_OUT="$(
        ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$_E2E_S10_STATE" \
        ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$_E2E_S10_EVDIR" \
        ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$_E2E_S10_EVDIR/events.jsonl" \
        ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
        ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0 \
        ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
        bash "$_E2E_S10_INSTALL/core/pipeline/runner.sh" \
            --template simple --goal "e2e-spec10-unreadable" 2>&1
    )" || _E2E_S10_RC=$?

    # Restore permissions so cleanup_test_env can remove the directory.
    chmod 644 "$_E2E_S10_INSTALL/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/plugin.sh" 2>/dev/null || true

    if [[ "$_E2E_S10_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: unreadable plugin.sh causes pipeline to exit non-zero"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: unreadable plugin.sh must cause pipeline to exit non-zero" \
            "runner exited 0; expected non-zero when plugin.sh is chmod 000"
    fi

    if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_E2E_S10_OUT"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: pipeline output names unreadable plugin.sh as 'misconfigured'"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: pipeline output must name unreadable plugin.sh as 'misconfigured'" \
            "output did not contain 'misconfigured'; old code: no runner.sh gate; got: ${_E2E_S10_OUT:0:300}"
    fi

    if grep -q 'bash-parallel' <<< "$_E2E_S10_OUT"; then
        assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: pipeline output names the misconfigured backend 'bash-parallel'"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] e2e: pipeline output must name the misconfigured backend" \
            "output did not contain 'bash-parallel'; got: ${_E2E_S10_OUT:0:300}"
    fi
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/integration/orch-backend-misconfigured-test.sh
#
# SPEC-2 (#1801): Running with a backend configured as `sequential` (or any
# name that resolves to no plugin) fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the
# backend; the sequential fallback in `orch_load_backend` is removed.
#
# SPEC-4 (#1801): A configured backend plugin that is absent from the installed
# tree (not the checkout) fails the run as `misconfigured` naming the missing
# backend.
#
# SPEC-10 (#1801): A backend whose plugin directory is present but whose config
# file is unreadable (permissions, corrupt, or missing) fails the run as
# `misconfigured` naming the backend — tested from the installed tree.
#
# All three must FAIL on old code (which has the sequential fallback) and PASS
# on new code (which removes the fallback and returns 1 naming the backend).
#
# Old code behaviour under each SPEC:
#   SPEC-2: orch_load_backend "sequential" → hardcoded path to the fallback backend
#           via hardcoded path → sources it → returns 0.
#   SPEC-4: orch_load_backend "absent-backend" → _orch_find_backend_dir fails →
#           general sequential fallback fires → returns 0 with a warning.
#   SPEC-10: source on unreadable plugin.sh fails silently (no set -e in contract.sh) →
#            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 runs anyway → returns 0.
#
# New code: every case returns 1, _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED stays 0, and
# stderr names the backend.
#
# [#1801/SPEC-2] [#1801/SPEC-4] [#1801/SPEC-10]
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "orch_load_backend fails misconfigured naming backend when fallback removed (#1801 SPEC-2,4,10)"
setup_test_env "orch-backend-misconfigured"

# Prevent auto-config-file reads from picking up the project's real config.
export ZBUILD_CONFIG_FILE="/dev/null"
export ZBUILD_PROJECT_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/project"

# Source contract.sh — it auto-calls _orch_load_backend at end.
# With ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT pointing at an empty dir and no zbuild_config_get_backend
# available, it defaults to "sequential" and:
#   old code: sources the fallback backend via hardcoded _ZBUILD_ROOT path → BACKEND_LOADED=1
#   new code: no fallback → orch_load_backend returns 1 (silenced by || true) → BACKEND_LOADED=0
# We reset _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0 before each SPEC section so the
# explicit call we are testing starts from a clean state.
_EMPTY_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/empty-plugins"
mkdir -p "$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
export ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND="sequential"

# shellcheck source=../../core/orch/contract.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/core/orch/contract.sh"

# ── SPEC-2: "sequential" name resolves to no plugin (fallback removed) ───────
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' fails when sequential fallback is removed"

_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
_SPEC2_ERR=""
_SPEC2_RC=0
_SPEC2_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "sequential" 2>&1)" || _SPEC2_RC=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC2_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' returns non-zero (sequential fallback removed)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] orch_load_backend 'sequential' must return non-zero (sequential fallback removed)" \
        "returned 0; old code finds the fallback backend via hardcoded _ZBUILD_ROOT path and sources it"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (backend correctly not loaded)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 when backend failed to load" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code sets it after sourcing the hardcoded sequential path"
fi

if grep -q 'sequential' <<< "$_SPEC2_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] error output names the backend 'sequential'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] error output must name the backend 'sequential'" \
        "stderr did not contain 'sequential'; got: ${_SPEC2_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# The run must be reported as `misconfigured` (not a generic failure).
# New code emits "misconfigured" in its error message or sets
# _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured; old code silently succeeds
# so this never reaches a misconfigured path at all.
if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC2_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-2] backend failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-2] backend failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC2_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# ── SPEC-4: absent backend plugin fails naming the missing backend ─────────────
# Backend name that is not present in the empty ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT and has no
# hardcoded fallback. Old code falls back to sequential silently; new code fails.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin fails naming backend (no general fallback)"

_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_EMPTY_PLUGINS"
_SPEC4_ERR=""
_SPEC4_RC=0
_SPEC4_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "orch-absent-spec4" 2>&1)" || _SPEC4_RC=$?

if [[ "$_SPEC4_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin returns non-zero (no fallback)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] orch_load_backend absent plugin must return non-zero (no fallback)" \
        "returned 0; old code's general sequential fallback fires for any missing backend"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (absent backend)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 for absent backend" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code's general fallback to sequential sets it"
fi

if grep -q 'orch-absent-spec4' <<< "$_SPEC4_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] error output names the missing backend 'orch-absent-spec4'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] error output must name the missing backend 'orch-absent-spec4'" \
        "stderr: ${_SPEC4_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC4_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-4] absent backend failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-4] absent backend failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC4_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

# ── SPEC-10: present dir, unreadable plugin.sh — fails naming the backend ─────
# Plugin directory and manifest are present (discovery succeeds) but plugin.sh
# is unreadable (chmod 000), simulating a corrupt or permission-denied install.
#
# Old code: source on unreadable file fails silently (no set -e in contract.sh),
#   then sets _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 and returns 0.
# New code: detects source failure, returns 1 naming the backend.
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend unreadable plugin.sh fails naming backend"

_S10_PLUGINS="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/spec10-plugins"
_S10_PLUGIN_DIR="$_S10_PLUGINS/tool/orch-broken-spec10"
mkdir -p "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR"
cat > "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/manifest.yaml" <<'MANIFEST'
id: orch-broken-spec10
name: Broken Backend Spec10
kind: tool
version: 0.0.1
provides:
  role: orchestrator-backend
  alias: orch-broken-spec10
MANIFEST
# Write a syntactically valid plugin.sh then remove read permission.
printf 'orch_spawn() { return 0; }\norch_capabilities() { printf '"'"'{}'"'"'; }\n' \
    > "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"
chmod 000 "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh"

export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$_S10_PLUGINS"
_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
_SPEC10_ERR=""
_SPEC10_RC=0
_SPEC10_ERR="$(orch_load_backend "orch-broken-spec10" 2>&1)" || _SPEC10_RC=$?

# Restore permissions so cleanup_test_env can remove the directory.
chmod 644 "$_S10_PLUGIN_DIR/plugin.sh" 2>/dev/null || true

if [[ "$_SPEC10_RC" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend with unreadable plugin.sh returns non-zero"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] orch_load_backend with unreadable plugin.sh must return non-zero" \
        "returned 0; old code: source fails silently, _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1 runs anyway, returns 0"
fi

if [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is not 1 (unreadable plugin.sh)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED must not be 1 when plugin.sh unreadable" \
        "sentinel set to 1; old code sets it even when source fails"
fi

if grep -q 'orch-broken-spec10' <<< "$_SPEC10_ERR"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] error output names the backend 'orch-broken-spec10'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] error output must name the backend 'orch-broken-spec10'" \
        "stderr: ${_SPEC10_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

if grep -q 'misconfigured' <<< "$_SPEC10_ERR" || \
   [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION:-}" == "misconfigured" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-10] unreadable plugin.sh failure is reported as 'misconfigured'"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-10] unreadable plugin.sh failure must be reported as 'misconfigured'" \
        "neither error output nor _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION contained 'misconfigured'; got: ${_SPEC10_ERR:-<empty>}"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration test (#1829, ADR-054 §7): the runner dispatches cleanup(release)
# on EVERY exit path from a run — success, non-zero rc, the SIGINT propagation
# chain, an external SIGTERM, and an external timeout.
#
# This is the acceptance criterion the mechanism exists for: a stage's live
# resources must be freed however the run ends. A single missed exit path leaks
# whatever that stage spawned (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Why SIGINT is driven by the stage rather than `kill -INT`: this harness starts
# non-interactively with SIGINT inherited as SIG_IGN, and POSIX forbids a child
# from un-ignoring it — so `kill -INT` is silently dropped and the assertion
# would pass standalone while proving nothing. The repo's existing
# sigint-aborts-pipeline-test.sh drives the same chain the same way: the child
# returns 130, which is exactly what the kernel produces on Ctrl-C. Since #1850
# (ADR-054 §4, ADR-025) a signal is a recorded WORD, not an rc, so the stage
# also arms the abort sentinel (empty = sigint), as the runner's INT trap in
# the process group would.
#
# Assertion in every case: the stub stages' cleanup hooks recorded `release`
# (and never `purge`) in the marker file.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "runner dispatches cleanup(release) on every exit path (#1829)"
setup_test_env "runner-release-exit-paths"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT"

# The teardown plugin resolves its repo root by walking three levels up from
# its own directory (plugin-bootstrap), using a LOGICAL pwd — so symlinking the
# plugin itself would resolve to TEST_TEMP_DIR and fail to find helpers.sh.
# Give TEST_TEMP_DIR the shape of a repo root instead, then copy teardown in.
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/scripts" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/scripts"
ln -s "$REPO_ROOT/core"    "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/core"
mkdir -p "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool"
cp -R "$REPO_ROOT/plugins/tool/teardown" "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown"

mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "test"   "tool"  0 >/dev/null

# Declare the optional cleanup hook — without it plugin_hook_call emits
# `plugin.cleanup.absent`, returns 0 (#1823: rc is binary), and the stage is a
# no-op rather than a witness.
# Re-emit the manifest rather than appending: `cleanup:` has to sit inside the
# contiguous `hooks:` block, and mock_plugin_factory already wrote `requires:`
# after it. #1850/#2366: the re-emitted manifest keeps the factory's declaration —
# result_contract 3 and a JSON primary each run hook below writes.
for _spec in "agent/intake:intake:intake_cleanup" "agent/build:build:build_cleanup" "tool/test:test:test_cleanup"; do
    _dir="${_spec%%:*}"; _rest="${_spec#*:}"; _id="${_rest%%:*}"; _fn="${_rest#*:}"
    _kind="${_dir%%/*}"
    cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/$_dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $_id
name: Test $_id
kind: $_kind
version: 0.0.1
hooks:
  run: ${_id//-/_}_run
  cleanup: $_fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
provides:
  result_contract: 3
outputs:
  - id: ${_id//-/_}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${_id}-result.json
    type: ${_id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
EOF
done

# Stubs: run honours env-driven rc/sleep; cleanup records "<stage>:<scope>".
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
intake_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/intake-result.json"
    return 0
}
intake_cleanup() { printf 'intake:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/build/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
build_run() {
    printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" > "${BUILD_STARTED:-/dev/null}"
    if [[ "${BUILD_SLEEP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        local _i; for _i in $(seq 1 300); do sleep 0.1; done
    fi
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    [[ "${BUILD_ARM_ABORT:-0}" == "1" ]] && : > "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal"
    if [[ "${BUILD_RC:-0}" == "0" ]]; then
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    else
        printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"broken","reason":"stub failure"}' > "$_art/build-result.json"
    fi
    return "${BUILD_RC:-0}"
}
build_cleanup() {
    printf 'build:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    # A hook that never returns — used to prove the dispatch is bounded. It
    # records its own pid so SPEC-6 can check it does not outlive the run (#2287).
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook.pid"
        sleep 120
    fi
    if [[ "${BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
        # #2333: a child that ignores TERM, under a hook shell that does not.
        ( trap '' TERM; printf '%s\n' "$BASHPID" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER%/*}/hook-child.pid"; sleep 120 ) &
        wait
    fi
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/test/plugin.sh" <<'PLUG'
test_run() {
    local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"
    printf '%s' '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"stub"}' > "$_art/test-result.json"
    return 0
}
test_cleanup() { printf 'test:%s\n' "${3:-NOSCOPE}" >> "${RELEASE_MARKER}"; return 0; }
PLUG

OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo release-exit-paths-repo)"
install_template_overlay "$OVERLAY_REPO" resume-minimal
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

_case_no=0
# _prep <name> — fresh state dir + marker for one exit path.
_prep() {
    _case_no=$((_case_no + 1))
    CASE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-$_case_no-$1"
    mkdir -p "$CASE_DIR/state" "$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$CASE_DIR/state"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$CASE_DIR/events"
    export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$CASE_DIR/events/events.jsonl"
    export RELEASE_MARKER="$CASE_DIR/release-marker"
    export BUILD_STARTED="$CASE_DIR/build-started"
    : > "$RELEASE_MARKER"
    unset BUILD_RC BUILD_SLEEP BUILD_ARM_ABORT 2>/dev/null || true
}

# _assert_released <case> <stage>... — EVERY named stage released, purge never.
#
# #1989: this used to grep the shared marker for any ':release' and pass. Three
# stages append to that one file, so one stage releasing masked two that never
# did — measured: neutering build_cleanup alone left the suite green, and it
# took neutering all three to turn it red. The assertion could only ever detect
# a TOTAL failure of the mechanism, never a partial one, which is the shape a
# real regression takes (#1748: suites observed alive 15+ min after exit).
#
# Each case now names the stages whose cleanup must have run. The sets differ
# by exit path because a stage only reaches release once it has been dispatched.
#
# ADR-062 §2: reclamation reads the process group recorded at DISPATCH, not the
# completion status map, so a stage killed mid-flight IS reclaimable. SPEC-4 and
# SPEC-5 therefore expect `build` as well as `intake` — build had demonstrably
# started (it wrote BUILD_STARTED) before the signal landed. Before #2001 both
# freed `intake` only, because teardown iterated `.stage_statuses`, which
# `_update_stage_status` writes only on complete/failed — i.e. after a stage
# returns, which a killed stage never does.
_assert_released() {
    local _case="$1"; shift
    local _marker; _marker="$(cat "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local _stage _missing=""
    for _stage in "$@"; do
        grep -q "^${_stage}:release$" <<< "$_marker" || _missing="${_missing}${_stage} "
    done
    if [[ -z "$_missing" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*"
    else
        assert_fail "[$_case] cleanup dispatched with scope=release for: $*" \
            "no release from: ${_missing}| marker=$(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_marker")"
    fi
    if grep -q ':purge' <<< "$_marker"; then
        assert_fail "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run" "marker contained purge"
    else
        assert_pass "[$_case] purge is never reachable from a run"
    fi
}

# SPEC-6 and SPEC-6b each wait out the release bound on purpose: their hook
# blocks, and the bound (the base template's release `timeout_s:` at the
# top-level stage block, 30s after #1801) is what ends it. Started here, each
# from its own repo, so that bound runs while SPEC-1..5 do; their assertions
# are made below, in order.
#
# SPEC-5 (#1801): a separate blocking run uses a template with timeout_s: 5
# for release (NOT router.timeout_s: 5) — old code reads router.timeout_s: 30
# and takes ~30s; new code reads template_stage_time_limit (timeout_s: 5) and
# exits in ~5s. Started here so it runs in parallel with SPEC-6/6b.
_start_blocking() {   # <case name> <hook switch> [template-id]
    local _repo; _repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-$1")"
    install_template_overlay "$_repo" resume-minimal
    local _tpl="${3:-resume-minimal}"
    (
        _prep "$1"
        export BUILD_RC=0 "$2"=1
        _t0=$(date +%s)
        ( cd "$_repo" && bash "$RUNNER" --template "$_tpl" --goal "release-$1" ) \
            >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 || true
        printf '%s\n' "$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))" > "$CASE_DIR/elapsed"
    ) &
}
_start_blocking blocking BLOCK_CLEANUP;                   _SPEC6_PID=$!
_start_blocking blocking-ignore-term BLOCK_CLEANUP_IGNORE_TERM; _SPEC6B_PID=$!
_SPEC6_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking"
_SPEC6B_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-blocking-ignore-term"

# [#1801/SPEC-5]: blocking run with timeout_s: 5 for release (top-level, read
# by template_stage_time_limit), while router.timeout_s: 30 is inherited from
# simple — distinguishes new code (uses timeout_s: 5) from old (router.timeout_s: 30).
_spec5_bound_repo="$(setup_git_temp_repo "release-exit-paths-spec5-bound")"
install_template_overlay "$_spec5_bound_repo" resume-minimal
if [[ -d "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info" ]] && \
   ! grep -qxF '/.zbuild/' "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude" 2>/dev/null; then
    printf '/.zbuild/\n' >> "$_spec5_bound_repo/.git/info/exclude"
fi
cat > "$_spec5_bound_repo/.zbuild/templates/resume-spec5-bound.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: resume-spec5-bound
extends: resume-minimal
release:
  timeout_s: 5
YAML
_start_blocking spec5-bound BLOCK_CLEANUP resume-spec5-bound; _SPEC5_BOUND_PID=$!
_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/case-1-spec5-bound"

# ── SPEC-1: success ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-1: exit path = success (rc 0)"
_prep success
export BUILD_RC=0
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-success" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# SPEC-6/6b run alongside this case; if it fails, say what the runner said.
[[ $_rc -eq 0 ]] || tail -20 "$CASE_DIR/out" >&2
assert_eq "[SPEC-1] runner exits 0 on the success path" "0" "$_rc"
_assert_released "SPEC-1" intake build test

# ── SPEC-2: non-zero stage rc ────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-2: exit path = non-zero stage rc"
_prep nonzero
export BUILD_RC=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-nonzero" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
if [[ "$_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-2] runner exits non-zero when a stage fails" "rc=0"
fi
_assert_released "SPEC-2" intake build

# ── SPEC-3: SIGINT propagation chain (child rc=130 + abort word) ─────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-3: exit path = SIGINT chain (stage rc 130, sentinel armed)"
_prep sigint
export BUILD_RC=130 BUILD_ARM_ABORT=1
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && bash "$RUNNER" --template resume-minimal --goal "release-sigint" ) \
    >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1
_rc=$?
set -e
# #1850: the run really took the SIGINT path — exit 1 (not 130) and the abort
# named sigint — or this case would only repeat SPEC-2's non-zero rc.
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] runner exits 1 on the SIGINT chain (not 130)" "1" "$_rc"
assert_eq "[SPEC-3] pipeline.aborted carries reason=sigint" "sigint" \
    "$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.aborted") | .data.reason // empty' "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr -d '\n')"
_assert_released "SPEC-3" intake build

# ── SPEC-4: external SIGTERM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "SPEC-4: exit path = external SIGTERM"
_prep sigterm
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
else
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-sigterm" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
fi
for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
_build_pid="$(head -n 1 "$BUILD_STARTED" 2>/dev/null || true)"
_t0=$(date +%s)
kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))
# ADR-054 §7: the runner acts on the signal while the stage is still running.
# Build holds for 30s; a runner that waits for it to return took 30s+ here.
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 15 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage (${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the runner stops without waiting for the stage" "took ${_elapsed}s; build holds 30s"
fi
if [[ -n "$_build_pid" ]] && kill -0 "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run" "build pid $_build_pid still alive"
    kill -KILL "$_build_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-4] the stage does not outlive the run"
fi
# The EXIT trap dispatches release asynchronously w.r.t. this shell's `wait`
# on some platforms; give the marker a bounded moment to appear.
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
_assert_released "SPEC-4" intake build

# ── SPEC-5: external hard kill (what an overrunning `timeout` produces) ──────
# ADR-053 §2: assert on an observable event, never a wall-clock budget.
#
# This case used to run the whole runner under `timeout 6`. Those 6 seconds had
# to cover process startup, template resolution AND reaching the build stage —
# so the budget was really a bet on host speed. Under the parallel pool (#991,
# the tier is parallel by default and the serial-pin list is empty) startup
# alone outran it: the runner was killed before any stage dispatched, the marker
# came back empty, and the failure read as a cleanup regression that standalone
# runs could never reproduce.
#
# The supervising timeout stays, but only as a runaway guard with a ceiling no
# healthy run approaches. The kill that this case actually asserts on is driven
# from BUILD_STARTED — the runner is provably inside the build stage — and
# escalates TERM→KILL the way `timeout` itself does, which is what separates
# this case from SPEC-4's plain SIGTERM.
print_test_section "SPEC-5: exit path = external hard kill (timeout-style)"
_prep timeout
export BUILD_RC=0 BUILD_SLEEP=1
_tbin=""
if   command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=gtimeout
elif command -v timeout  >/dev/null 2>&1; then _tbin=timeout
fi
if [[ -z "$_tbin" ]]; then
    SKIP=$((SKIP + 1))
    echo -e "  ${YELLOW}SKIP${RESET}: [SPEC-5] external hard kill (no timeout binary available)" >&2
else
    # #2029: the force-kill grace must be DERIVED from the release budget, not a
    # hardcoded literal. _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT is the per-stage bound (after #1801
    # this is template_stage_time_limit — 30s in simple.yaml; 3s here is a
    # test-safe stand-in). Three stages release on this path, so the grace clears
    # 3x the per-hook bound. The hooks in this case return promptly; the grace is
    # only a runaway guard so a runner that ignores TERM cannot hang the suite.
    _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT=3
    _SPEC5_KILL_GRACE=$(( _SPEC5_STAGE_TIMEOUT * 3 + 6 ))   # 3 stages + margin
    set -m
    bash -c 'cd "$1" && exec "$4" 120 bash "$2" --template resume-minimal --goal "$3"' \
        _ "$OVERLAY_REPO" "$RUNNER" "release-timeout" "$_tbin" >"$CASE_DIR/out" 2>&1 &
    RUNNER_PID=$!
    set +m
    for _ in $(seq 1 300); do [[ -s "$BUILD_STARTED" ]] && break; sleep 0.1; done
    kill -TERM -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -TERM "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    ( sleep "$_SPEC5_KILL_GRACE"; kill -KILL -"$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || kill -KILL "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true ) &
    _spec5_killer=$!
    wait "$RUNNER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
    kill "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    wait "$_spec5_killer" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do grep -q ':release' "$RELEASE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.1; done
    _assert_released "SPEC-5" intake build
fi

# ── SPEC-6: a blocking cleanup hook cannot hold the exit open ────────────────
# The dispatch runs inside the EXIT trap, so an unbounded hook would turn a
# normal exit into a hang — the same class of bug (a process that outlives the
# run) that this mechanism exists to prevent.
print_test_section "SPEC-6: a cleanup hook that blocks cannot hang the runner"
wait "$_SPEC6_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6_DIR"
_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
# The blocking hook sleeps 120s. The bound is the release stage's own
# `timeout_s:` at the top-level stage block (read by template_stage_time_limit
# after #1801 — 30s in simple.yaml), so the runner returns in about 30s.
# Allow generous headroom for a loaded host while still failing an unbounded wait.
if [[ "$_elapsed" -lt 60 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded (runner exited in ${_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] blocking cleanup is bounded" "runner took ${_elapsed}s"
fi
# #2287: the bound must stop the hook, not just stop waiting for it. Before,
# the hook lived on after the run, finished its sleep ~2 min later, and wrote
# into a state folder the run no longer owned. The kills are sent before the
# runner returns; up to 1s covers the killed processes exiting on a loaded host.
_hook_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 10); do kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_hook_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] fixture: the blocking hook recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook.pid"
elif kill -0 "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run" "pid $_hook_pid still alive after the runner returned"
    # Leave nothing behind for the rest of the suite: the hook first, so it
    # cannot carry on once its sleep ends, then the sleep it leaves orphaned.
    _hook_kids="$(pgrep -P "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    kill -KILL "$_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    for _k in $_hook_kids; do kill -KILL "$_k" 2>/dev/null || true; done
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6] the blocked hook does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── SPEC-6b (#2333): a child that ignores TERM is killed too ────────────────
# The bound sends TERM to the hook's group, then KILL after a grace. The runner
# waited only for the group leader and cancelled the watchdog when it exited, so
# a member that ignored TERM never got the KILL and outlived the run.
print_test_section "SPEC-6b: a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
# The time bound itself is SPEC-6's check, on the same dispatch path; this
# case is only about what survives it.
wait "$_SPEC6B_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC6B_DIR"
_child_pid=""
for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
    _child_pid="$(head -n 1 "$CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]] && break; sleep 0.1
done
_alive=1
# Only poll a pid that was recorded; a missing pid is reported as a fixture failure below.
if [[ -n "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    for _ in $(seq 1 50); do kill -0 "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || { _alive=0; break; }; sleep 0.1; done
fi
if [[ -z "$_child_pid" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] fixture: the child recorded its pid" "no $CASE_DIR/hook-child.pid"
elif [[ "$_alive" -eq 1 ]]; then
    assert_fail "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run" "pid $_child_pid still alive 5s after the runner returned"
    kill -KILL "$_child_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
else
    assert_pass "[SPEC-6b] a hook child that ignores TERM does not outlive the run"
fi

# ── [#1801/SPEC-5]: _runner_dispatch_always_run uses template_stage_time_limit ──
# A blocking hook under a template with `timeout_s: 5` for release (top-level)
# must stop in ~5s, NOT in ~30s (router.timeout_s: 30 inherited from simple).
# Old code reads _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_release (router.timeout_s = 30) and
# uses that as the watchdog → runner takes ~30s.
# New code reads template_stage_time_limit("release") = 5 → runner takes ~5s.
# Assertion at < 20s: FAILS on old code (~30s), PASSES on new code (~5s).
print_test_section "[#1801/SPEC-5]: always-run watchdog bound by timeout_s: (not router.timeout_s)"
wait "$_SPEC5_BOUND_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
CASE_DIR="$_SPEC5_BOUND_DIR"
_spec5_elapsed="$(cat "$CASE_DIR/elapsed" 2>/dev/null || echo 999)"
if [[ "$_spec5_elapsed" -lt 20 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5 (runner exited in ${_spec5_elapsed}s; would be ~30s with router.timeout_s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] always-run watchdog uses timeout_s: 5" \
        "runner took ${_spec5_elapsed}s — expected < 20s (timeout_s: 5); old code would use router.timeout_s: 30"
fi

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT must not appear in runner.sh.
# Old code reads ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT for the always-run watchdog; new code reads
# template_stage_time_limit instead. This grep fails on old code (the var is there)
# and passes on new code (it has been removed).
if ! grep -q 'ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT (removed in #1801)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT" \
        "ZBUILD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
fi

# [#1801/SPEC-5] static guard: _runner_dispatch_always_run must not reference
# router.timeout_s (its bash manifestation: _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_*).
# Old code (runner.sh): local _ar_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT_${_ar_safe}"
# which reads router.timeout_s from the template config.
# New code: reads template_stage_time_limit instead.
# This grep fails on old code (the string is present) and passes on new (removed).
if ! grep -q '_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT' "$RUNNER"; then
    assert_pass "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh does not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s removed from always-run watchdog in #1801)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1801/SPEC-5] runner.sh must not reference _TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT (router.timeout_s)" \
        "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
fi

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

lines: "_TPL_STAGE_ROUTER_TIMEOUT still present in $RUNNER; must be replaced by template_stage_time_limit"
+# [#1801/SPEC-5] static: shipped templates carry timeout_s: at stage level ──────
+# template_stage_time_limits_load reads timeout_s: at stage-level indent (2
+# spaces from the stage name at column 0, NOT inside `router:` at 4 spaces).
